svg.title: Precision envelope detector: an op-amp removes the diode drop
svg.desc: A precision envelope detector. The AM input goes to the non-inverting input of an op-amp. The op-amp output drives a diode D, whose other end is the output node, with a capacitor C and a resistor R in parallel to ground. A feedback wire runs from the output node back to the op-amp's inverting input, so the op-amp drives the diode until the output equals the input, and the diode's forward drop is divided by the op-amp's gain. Below, two simulated outputs for the same weak AM input, a 1 volt carrier with 50 percent modulation: a plain silicon diode detector with a 0.6 volt drop loses the troughs completely and its output is far below the envelope; the precision detector follows the envelope.
svg.text: feedback: the op-amp drives D until output = input
Simulated output (orange) for a weak AM input (blue, 1 V carrier, 50% modulation), true envelope dashed
